text.p: A smiling Mother Teresa walked out of hospital on Thursday, three weeks after undergoing her third heart operation in five years, and returned to her religious order.

The 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun walked unaided out of the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre and, smiling with her hands clasped together in the traditional Indian greeting, bowed to the crowd of people waiting outside the hospital.
She was accompanied by doctors and Sister Fredrica, second in command at the Missionaries of Charity religious order.
Doctors said special arrangements had been made at the Missionaries of Charity to monitor Mother Teresa's heart.

The revered Roman Catholic missionary, fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, was taken to hospital on November 22 after suffering heart failure. It was the third time since August that she had been admitted to hospital for emergency care.
Doctors operated on her on November 29, unblocking two coronary arteries with a tiny balloon. The surgery, during which she was under general anaesthesia, was successful.
But a faltering heartbeat and long-standing lung and kidney problems delayed her recovery. Twice in the past week doctors have given her a mild electric shock to correct her heartbeat.
On Wednesday doctors said nagging bronchitis, which has periodically dogged Mother Teresa from her youth, had finally cleared up.
The 1979 Nobel peace prize winner had been pressing doctors to let her return to her religious order.
Doctors have said Mother Teresa may never regain her full strength after her latest stay in hospital or be as active as she was in the past.
